name: Ashpile Stitch-Thermal Underlayer
description: Hand-stitched from salvaged insulation batting, reclaimed synth-fleece strips, and scavenged thermal foil remnants, this underlayer is a patchwork of mismatched gray, rust, and industrial yellow. Every seam is doubled by hand with waxed thread — some sections re-stitched three or four times over. The surface is uneven, lumpy in places, but it holds heat against Shelf cold and acid-rain damp with stubborn efficiency. Worn edges are bound with whatever ribbon or cord was available.
functionality: Passive thermal retention against sub-zero Shelf temperatures and acid-rain moisture; no smart features, no power draw — just layered insulation that works when the grid doesn't.
what_it_says: You make do with what the city throws away, and you've gotten very good at it.
worn_by: kids who inherited their parents' patch jobs
story_hooks: A distinctive patch of orange industrial foil matches a scrap found at a sealed-off collapse site — someone was there when the building came down.
The inner lining contains a hand-sewn pocket with a folded paper note in a language the wearer can't read.
A Shelf kid trades one of these to a Tier 3 journalist who's going undercover — it's the most honest thing they've ever worn.
